pages.text: The pack ships graphics profiles by $(bold)hardware$(). Pick yours in-game with $(bold)/peacock profile <tier>$() and relaunch; the launcher applies it. (In Prism the PEACOCK_PROFILE variable still works as a fallback; CurseForge players pick the tier by which zip they install.)

$(li)$(bold)potato:$() integrated graphics, an old or hot laptop; shaders off$(li)$(bold)low$() (the default): integrated graphics with headroom, a fanless MacBook Air; Complementary at its lightest$(li)$(bold)medium:$() a thin laptop with a fan$(li)$(bold)high:$() a laptop with a real GPU$(li)$(bold)ultra:$() a desktop with a dedicated GPU
pages.title: The tiers

pages.text: Anything you change in the video or shader menus is kept; the profile only sets defaults. Shaders toggle with $(bold)K$(). If frames drop: lower Distant Horizons' radius first, shaders second, render distance last.$(br2)Macs stay on plain Complementary; the Euphoria variant exceeds what macOS OpenGL offers.

$(bold)Distant Horizons$() draws the far terrain from a low-detail copy the server builds as players explore. On a fresh world the horizon fills in over the first hour; a reset world starts over.$(br2)Embeddium, ImmediatelyFast, Entity Culling, ModernFix and FerriteCore are the quiet half of the frame rate; leave them on. Sound Physics (cave echo) is off on potato. Particle mods can be turned down in their menus.

$(bold)Resource packs$() are on by default: Fresh Animations (+ Details, Objects), Optimized Bushy Leaves over Better Leaves, Fast Better Grass, rainbow's foliage, 3D Default, Cubic Sun & Moon, Enhanced Boss Bars, xali's books and potions, Low on Fire.$(br2)All optional (Options, Resource Packs). Potato leaves out 3D Default and the Fresh Animations family. Smooth Steps eases the camera up each slab and block you step onto.
